links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4 prostate cancer patient education responses versus appropriate reading level
links.effect: Consensus 'difficult to read'; Flesch Reading Ease mean 45.97, Gunning Fog 14.55, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 12.12, averaging an 11th-grade reading level.
links.quote: The readability algorithm consensus was "difficult to read" (Flesch Reading Ease score mean 45.97, SD 8.69; Gunning Fog Index mean 14.55, SD 4.79), averaging an 11th-grade reading level, equivalent to 15- to 17-year-olds (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level mean 12.12, SD 4.34; The Coleman-Liau Index mean 12.75, SD 1.98; SMOG Index mean 11.06, SD 3.20).

links.outcome: Reference hallucination and quality of citations in ChatGPT-4 outputs
links.effect: REF-AI identified 2 reference hallucinations; 28/30 (93%) references appropriately supplemented text; 26/30 (86%) from reputable government organizations.
links.quote: REF-AI identified 2 reference hallucinations, while the majority (28/30, 93%) of references appropriately supplemented the text.

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT-4's performance (quality, accuracy, readability, hallucination rate) on patient education questions about prostate cancer, evaluated by expert clinicians offline without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
